blocks.text: Chain of thought prompting asks a model to work through its reasoning step by step before giving a final answer, rather than jumping straight to a conclusion, this simple shift measurably improves accuracy on problems that genuinely require multiple reasoning steps to solve correctly.

This topic opens the Advanced Prompting Techniques module, covering why explicit reasoning steps help, the zero-shot and few-shot variants of the technique, where it helps most, and its real cost in extra tokens and response time.
1. What Chain of Thought Prompting Means

blocks.alt: What Chain of Thought Prompting Means
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473222101-225350267.png

Chain of thought, commonly abbreviated CoT, means prompting a model to lay out its intermediate reasoning steps explicitly before stating a final answer, rather than producing just the answer directly.
2. Why Explicit Reasoning Steps Improve Accuracy

blocks.alt: Why Explicit Reasoning Steps Improve Accuracy
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473222101-488516082.png

This connects directly back to the generation mechanics covered in the earlier How LLMs Process Prompts topic, a model generates one token at a time, conditioned on everything generated so far, working through reasoning steps first gives the model a chance to build toward a correct answer incrementally, rather than needing to produce a complex correct answer in one immediate leap.

code.content:
# Without CoT
"What is 47 times 23? Answer with just the number."

# With CoT
"What is 47 times 23? Show your work step by step, then give the final answer."

blocks.text: 3. Zero-Shot CoT vs Few-Shot CoT
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473222102-659354916.png

Zero-shot CoT is remarkably simple, appending a phrase like "think step by step" to an otherwise ordinary prompt, few-shot CoT, building on the few-shot prompting technique covered in the previous module, goes further, showing one or more complete worked examples of the reasoning process itself, not just the final answer.

blocks.content: {"headers":["CoT Variant","What Gets Added to the Prompt"],"rows":[["Zero-shot CoT","A simple instruction like think step by step"],["Few-shot CoT","A full worked example showing the reasoning chain"]]}

blocks.text: 4. Where Chain of Thought Helps Most

blocks.alt: Where Chain of Thought Helps Most
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473222103-645193272.png

CoT provides the largest benefit on tasks genuinely requiring multiple dependent reasoning steps, multi step arithmetic, logic puzzles, and problems where an intermediate result feeds into a later step, tasks a model can otherwise skip past too quickly when asked only for a direct final answer.
5. Where Chain of Thought Adds Little Value

For simple factual lookups or single step tasks, what is the capital of France, CoT adds unnecessary length without any real accuracy benefit, the technique earns its value specifically on problems with real intermediate reasoning to walk through.
6. The Real Cost, More Tokens and Slower Responses

blocks.alt: The Real Cost, More Tokens and Slower Responses
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473222103-891848554.png

CoT responses are longer, consuming more output tokens, covered in the earlier Tokens and Tokenization topic, and taking measurably longer to generate, this cost is worth paying specifically when the accuracy improvement on a genuinely complex task outweighs the added latency and expense.

blocks.title: This is a real, quantifiable tradeoff worth measuring
blocks.content: Applying CoT indiscriminately to every single request in a high volume production system can noticeably increase both cost and latency, reserving it for tasks that actually benefit is a more deliberate, cost aware approach.

blocks.text: 7. Separating Reasoning From the Final Answer

blocks.alt: Separating Reasoning From the Final Answer
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473222104-687219969.png

A practical detail matters here, explicitly asking the model to mark its final answer clearly, "Final answer:", makes it much easier for an application to programmatically extract just the answer from a response that also includes the full reasoning trace.
8. CoT Reliability Is Not Perfect

Chain of thought improves accuracy on many reasoning tasks, but the reasoning steps a model produces are not a guaranteed, verified proof, a model can still produce reasoning that looks plausible but contains a subtle error, CoT reduces certain classes of mistakes without eliminating error entirely.
9. Chain of Thought as a Foundation for More Advanced Techniques

blocks.alt: Chain of Thought as a Foundation for More Advanced Techniques
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785473222453-671430454.png

The remaining topics in this module, self-consistency prompting, tree of thoughts, ReAct, and others, all build directly on this same core idea of making reasoning explicit, extending it with additional structure like exploring multiple reasoning paths or interleaving reasoning with real actions.
Worked Example

A developer building a math tutoring tool asks a model directly for the answer to a multi step word problem, the model occasionally gets the final number wrong despite the problem being solvable with careful arithmetic.

Adding "solve this step by step, showing each calculation, then state the final answer clearly" to the same prompt produces a visible reasoning trace, and the final answer accuracy improves noticeably across a batch of similar test problems, since the model now works through the problem incrementally rather than attempting to leap directly to a final number.
Common Mistakes

items: Applying chain of thought to every request indiscriminately, including simple tasks that gain no real benefit from it
Not asking the model to clearly mark its final answer, making the response harder to parse programmatically
Assuming a plausible looking reasoning trace guarantees a correct final answer
Ignoring the added token cost and latency CoT introduces when applying it at high volume in production

blocks.text: Practice

Take a multi step reasoning problem, a word problem or logic puzzle, and prompt a model for it both with a direct answer only request and with an explicit step by step CoT request, comparing the accuracy and length of each response.
Key Takeaway

Chain of thought prompting asks a model to reason through intermediate steps explicitly before answering, meaningfully improving accuracy on genuinely multi step problems at the cost of longer, slower responses, and it forms the foundational idea the more advanced reasoning techniques covered in the rest of this module build on.
